newsitem.title: singapore: Asian crudes weaker, Dubai down, Tapis premium up.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weaker, Dubai down, Tapis premium up.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia were mostly weaker on Monday with Dubai noted for a 20-cent fall after only one Dubai cargo was awarded in the India tender.
Light sweet grades were boosted by an end-Jan Tapis cargo sold at a premium of $1.40 -- five cents above the last partial sold and 40 cents higher than the last full cargo sold.
A producer sold 550-600,000 barrels to a Singapore major. The last partial was done at $1.35 and the last cargo at $1.00.
The Tapis deal followed a January Cossack cargo sold Friday at a premium of 40 cents over Tapis, indicating strong demand from refiners for middle distillate yields amid positive margins.
However, traders said the buyer of the latest Tapis was a major that is short and needed to buy. The major was unavailable to comment.
Meanwhile, the weakness of futures on Friday prompted a slide in outright values for Asian crudes.
The one-cargo take-up of Dubai in the Indian tender dropped the Feb/Mar intermonth spread to 45/55 cents per barrel from 65/70 in Asia on Friday. Late New York indications on Friday were 70/80 cents.
The February Brent/Dubai spread widened out to $1.95/$2.00 from $1.85/$1.90.
The narrowing backwardation was likely to add value to Dubai-related grades, but traders said most of February was already placed.
